subject: Kuiper.ai: elevated errors & tail latency — exec review and credit proposal
messages:
From: Jared Liu <jared@kuiper.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn.moore <evelyn.moore@kuiper.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors & tail latency — urgent

Hi Naomi,

We saw a spike in error rates and 95th/99th percentile latency across our ingestion-heavy routes between 02:00 and 06:00 UTC last night. Throughput dropped ~25% and the SDK retries materially increased client-side CPU. Our SREs captured traces and there are persistent KV-cache misses correlated with longer context lengths.

This is the second time in six weeks we’ve had a multi-hour degradation window. The contract includes a 99.5% availability target with service credit language — we need to understand what happened, what compensation you’ll provide, and what guarantees you can give while we decide on renewal.

Please treat as high priority and loop in whoever you need. We’d like an executive-level call today if possible.

Thanks,
Jared
CRO, Kuiper.ai

---

What I want before the 4pm call:

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Kuiper.ai: elevated errors & tail latency — prep notes

Naomi — quick findings from initial triage:
- Correlation: multiple hosts in us-west-2 autoscale group hit sustained GC/IO backpressure during long-context multi-part requests; KV cache eviction rate spiked when request sizes exceeded the model profile (we saw a ~40% increase in KV read miss-rate).
- Root cause (hypothesis): a misapplied batching configuration combined with a recent scheduler tweak that favored throughput. Under certain request-size distributions, this increased latency variance and pushed some requests to timeout and retry.
- Immediate mitigation: revert the scheduler tweak and throttle large-batch windows for the affected pool (target: within 3 hours).
- Longer term: tune batching heuristics, add explicit large-context routing, and ship a telemetry guard to reject requests above a hard upper bound for the current pool.

I’ll push the revert to canary within 2 hours and monitor. Attaching a short CSV with SLO deltas.

—Rishi

Attachment: slo-dash-202608-report.csv (text/csv)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Liu <jared@kuiper.ai>, evelyn.moore <evelyn.moore@kuiper.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed remediation & credit calibration — Kuiper.ai incident 2026-09-01

Hi Jared / Evelyn — thank you for patience while our team investigated. Below is a consolidated update and a proposed commercial remediation.

Technical summary:
- Cause: batching/scheduler change + large-context request distribution resulted in high KV-cache miss-rate and IO pressure on a subset of our us-west-2 pool.
- Immediate action taken: reverted the scheduler change and deployed a canary throttle for large batches. Canary telemetry shows error rate reduced to baseline and p99 latency returning towards normal within 45 minutes of the revert.
- Next steps (operational fixes):
  - refine batching heuristics and add explicit routing for large-context requests (ETA: 10 business days)
  - implement telemetry guardrails with pre-reject and clearer error codes (ETA: 14 business days)
  - quarterly configuration review with your SREs (first session: 2026-09-21)

Commercial proposal (good-faith remediation):
- Service credit: 6% of monthly invoice for September 2026, applied as an account-level credit on your next invoice. This reflects the observed impact window and our SLA terms.
- One-time professional support: 8 hours of dedicated infra time to run joint tuning and verification (no charge).
- Contract amendment: we propose an explicit configuration review and a one-year SLA addendum clarifying large-context routing responsibilities and a shared rollback process. Draft attached.

Attachments: proposed-amendment-RedwoodKuiper_v2.docx, service-telemetry-20260901.zip, slo-dash-202608-report.csv

Ask from you:
- Can you confirm acceptance of the 6% credit and the joint tuning engagement?
- If yes, legal can route the amendment via DocuSign; if you prefer a different credit amount, propose and we can escalate.

If helpful, we can run a 30-minute executive recap tomorrow to walk through the proposed amendment and timelines.

Sincerely,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0112
